meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and when?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.

Fair would have been a phone call before the zero, and you still haven't told me who decided. A forty-minute in-class piece set against an essay he had time to work on shows he can revise, Hale. Show me the September 24 piece; I'll read it myself.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.

Then the checker was on the table when the zero went in, and now it isn't. You said "version history"; show me, with the times, and turn the screen so I can read it. Was Owen shown any of this before the zero was entered?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,
Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn, that you tell me who decided it and whether Owen was heard first, and that I see the September 24 piece and the version history myself. I expect your answer in writing.
Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and to read your evidence herself.
What moved her: dropping the checker and describing a dated, specific comparison with Owen's own in-class writing moved her slightly, because that is the kind of evidence she weighs, though she never got to see it.
What cost ground: never answering who decided the zero or owning that it went in before anyone called her, which kept her focused on process instead of the essay.
Try next time: open with one sentence owning that the zero was entered before you called her, then turn the screen and show her the September 24 writing and the version history with its times.
